name: Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
facts: Seat of the Archdiocese of Mobile, the oldest Catholic see on the U.S. Gulf Coast (est. as a diocese 1829).
Greek Revival building begun in 1835; its portico and twin towers were completed later in the 19th century.
Houses hand-painted German stained-glass windows and was designated a minor basilica in 1962.

name: St. Mary's Basilica
facts: The oldest Catholic parish in Phoenix, founded in 1881; the current church was completed in 1914.
Franciscan-run, it holds the largest collection of stained glass in Arizona.
Pope John Paul II visited in 1987, two years after its 1985 designation as a minor basilica.

name: Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi (Mission Dolores)
facts: Adjacent to Mission Dolores (1776), the oldest surviving structure in San Francisco.
The parish is the oldest in the city; the basilica church was built after the mission era.
Designated a minor basilica in 1952, among the first in the western United States.

name: Basilica of Mission San Carlos Borromeo (Carmel Mission)
facts: Founded in 1770 by St. Junípero Serra, who is buried at the mission and served as his headquarters.
The stone church, completed in 1797, is a landmark of Spanish colonial California architecture.
Designated a minor basilica in 1960; Serra was canonized in 2015.

name: St. Joseph Basilica
facts: Romanesque-style parish church completed in the early 20th century for a growing East Bay community.
Known for its ornate interior and twin bell towers overlooking Alameda.
Designated a minor basilica in 1972.

name: Mission Basilica San Diego de Alcalá
facts: The first of the 21 California missions, founded by St. Junípero Serra in 1769.
Site of California's first Christian burial ground and often called the 'Mother of the Missions.'
Designated a minor basilica in 1975.

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Joseph
facts: Seat of the Diocese of San José; the parish dates to 1803, the first non-mission parish in California.
The present domed, Italian Renaissance-style church was completed in 1877 after fires and earthquakes destroyed earlier ones.
Named a minor basilica by papal decree of December 1995; the title was formally conferred in 1997.

name: Mission Basilica San Juan Capistrano
facts: The mission was founded in 1776; its Great Stone Church was ruined by an 1812 earthquake.
The modern basilica church (2000) was built as a large-scale re-creation of the lost stone church.
Famed for the annual return of the swallows; designated a minor basilica in 2000.

name: Mission Basilica San Buenaventura
facts: The ninth and last mission founded personally by St. Junípero Serra, in 1782.
Its adobe church, completed in 1809, sits at the heart of downtown Ventura.
Elevated to a minor basilica in 2020.

credit.author: The original uploader was Geographer at English Wikipedia.

name: Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
facts: Seat of the Archdiocese of Denver; a French Gothic Revival landmark completed in 1911.
Its twin 210-foot spires and 75+ stained-glass windows are civic landmarks of Denver.
Pope John Paul II prayed here during World Youth Day 1993; designated a basilica in 1979.

name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
facts: Renaissance Revival church completed in 1928 for Waterbury's Catholic community.
Noted for its marble interior, murals, and large pipe organ.
Designated a minor basilica in 2008.

name: Basilica of St. John the Evangelist
facts: Twin-spired Gothic Revival church, a downtown Stamford landmark since the 1880s.
Serves one of the oldest Catholic parishes in the region.
Designated a minor basilica in 2009.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception
facts: The largest Roman Catholic church in North America and the U.S. patronal shrine of the Immaculate Conception.
Byzantine-Romanesque; built 1920–1959, its Great Dome and campanile dominate the skyline near Catholic University.
Designated a minor basilica in 1990; it contains dozens of chapels honoring Marian devotions worldwide.

credit.author: Jesus_Mountain.jpg: Joseph V derivative work: Rabanus Flavus

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Augustine
facts: Seat of the Diocese of St. Augustine; its parish (1565) is the oldest Catholic congregation in the United States.
The Spanish Colonial church was built in the 1790s and restored after an 1887 fire.
Designated a minor basilica in 1976.

name: Basilica of St. Paul
facts: Spanish Renaissance-style church with a prominent dome, completed in 1931.
A longtime landmark of downtown Daytona Beach.
Designated a minor basilica in 2006.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of Mary, Queen of the Universe
facts: Built to serve the millions of Catholic visitors to the Orlando/theme-park region.
One of very few basilicas conceived primarily as a shrine for tourists and pilgrims.
Designated a minor basilica in 2009.

name: Basilica of St. Michael the Archangel
facts: Traces to a Spanish colonial parish; Pensacola is among the oldest European settlements in the U.S.
The Gothic Revival church was completed in the late 19th century.
Designated a minor basilica in 2011.

name: Basilica of St. Mary Star of the Sea
facts: Founded in 1852; long the spiritual anchor of Catholic Key West.
Its grotto to Our Lady of Lourdes (1922) is said locally to protect the island from hurricanes.
Designated a minor basilica in 2012.

name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
facts: One of Jacksonville's oldest congregations, rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1901.
Gothic Revival church known for its stained glass.
Designated a minor basilica in 2013.

name: Basilica of St. Edward
facts: Spanish Renaissance-style church completed in 1927 in the resort town of Palm Beach.
President John F. Kennedy attended Mass here during stays at the Kennedy family home.
Designated a minor basilica in 2024.

name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
facts: One of Atlanta's oldest churches (1897–1898), built in Romanesque Revival style by Marist priests.
Twin spires make it a landmark of downtown Atlanta.
Designated a minor basilica in 2010.

credit.author: Warren LeMay from Cincinnati, OH, United States

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. John the Baptist
facts: Seat of the Diocese of Savannah; French Gothic, completed in 1896 and rebuilt after an 1898 fire.
Its twin spires and painted interior make it one of the South's most photographed churches.
Designated a minor basilica in 2020, one of the newest in the country.

name: Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
facts: Seat of the Diocese of Honolulu and one of the oldest cathedrals in continuous use in the U.S. (dedicated 1843).
St. Damien of Molokai was ordained a priest here in 1864.
Designated a minor basilica in 2014.

name: Our Lady of Sorrows Basilica
facts: Served by the Servite Order; a center of the Friday Sorrowful Mother Novena that spread nationwide in the 1930s–40s.
Grand Renaissance/Baroque interior completed in the early 20th century.
Designated a minor basilica in 1956, the first in Chicago.

credit.author: Original by w:User:JeremyA , edited version by w:User:Capital photographer

name: Queen of All Saints Basilica
facts: A Gothic Revival 'jewel box' completed in 1960 on Chicago's North Side.
Designed with elaborate stone tracery, statuary, and stained glass.
Designated a minor basilica in 1962, soon after its completion.

name: Basilica of St. Hyacinth
facts: A landmark of Chicago's Polish community, completed in 1921 in the Polish Cathedral style.
Its three towers and vast interior seat one of the largest congregations in the city.
Designated a minor basilica in 2003.

name: Basilica of St. Francis Xavier (Old Cathedral)
facts: Indiana's oldest parish, founded by Jesuit missionaries in 1734.
The 1826 brick church was the first cathedral of the Diocese of Vincennes.
Designated a minor basilica in 1970; its Old Cathedral Library holds rare early books.

name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart
facts: The church of the University of Notre Dame, completed in 1888 by the Congregation of Holy Cross.
Home to a renowned collection of murals and the oldest carillon in North America.
Designated a minor basilica in 1991.

name: Basilica of St. Francis Xavier
facts: A soaring Gothic Revival church built 1887–1889 by German Catholic settlers on the Iowa prairie.
Its twin 212-foot spires are visible for miles; often called 'the Cathedral of the Prairie.'
Designated a minor basilica in 1956, one of the first outside a major city.

name: Basilica of St. John the Apostle
facts: Romanesque church completed in 1927, a landmark of Des Moines.
Noted for its mosaics, marble, and a large central dome.
Designated a minor basilica in the late 20th century.

name: Basilica of St. Fidelis (Cathedral of the Plains)
facts: Built 1908–1911 by Volga-German immigrants; nicknamed the 'Cathedral of the Plains' by William Jennings Bryan.
Its twin 141-foot towers make it one of the largest churches in the Great Plains.
Constructed largely with hand-hauled native limestone by the parishioners themselves.

credit.author: Leo P. Hallak (changes by Rabanus Flavus)

name: Basilica of the Blessed Virgin of Gethsemani
facts: Church of the Abbey of Gethsemani (1848), the oldest Trappist monastery in the U.S.
Home of the writer-monk Thomas Merton, who lived and is buried here.
Designated a minor basilica in 1949.

name: Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption
facts: Seat of the Diocese of Covington; a French Gothic design modeled partly on Notre-Dame de Paris.
Contains one of the world's largest handmade stained-glass windows.
Designated a minor basilica in 1953.

name: St. Joseph Proto-Cathedral Basilica
facts: The first Catholic cathedral built west of the Appalachians (1816–1819).
Its art collection includes paintings gifted by European royalty and popes.
'Proto-cathedral' marks it as the mother church of the interior U.S.; designated a basilica in 2001.

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Louis, King of France
facts: The oldest continuously active Catholic cathedral in the United States; present church dedicated 1794.
Its triple-spired facade on Jackson Square is an icon of New Orleans.
Designated a minor basilica in 1964; Pope John Paul II visited in 1987.

credit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Krakers assumed (based on copyright claims). (Corrected by User:StAn)

name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
facts: Serves the oldest permanent settlement in the Louisiana Purchase (Natchitoches, founded 1714).
The present Romanesque church dates to the 1850s.
Designated a minor basilica in 2009.

name: Basilica of St. Stephen
facts: A towering Gothic Revival church completed in 1887 by the Vincentians.
Its steeple is among the tallest in New Orleans.
Designated a minor basilica in 2022.

name: Basilica of Sts. Peter and Paul
facts: A vast Gothic church built by French-Canadian mill workers, completed 1936.
One of the largest churches in New England, seating around 2,000.
Designated a minor basilica in 2004.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Assumption of the BVM
facts: The first Roman Catholic cathedral in the United States, built 1806–1821.
Designed by Benjamin Henry Latrobe, architect of the U.S. Capitol, in Neoclassical style.
Seat of the first U.S. diocese (Baltimore); designated a minor basilica in 1937.

credit.author: The original uploader was Basilica1 at English Wikipedia.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
facts: Enshrines the remains of St. Elizabeth Ann Seton, the first native-born U.S. citizen canonized a saint.
Adjoins the site where she founded the Sisters of Charity and American parochial schooling.
Designated a minor basilica in 1991.

name: Basilica & Shrine of Our Lady of Perpetual Help (Mission Church)
facts: Run by the Redemptorists; a Romanesque landmark in Roxbury completed in 1878, its towers added 1910.
Famous as a shrine of healing, with walls once lined with crutches left by pilgrims.
Designated a minor basilica in 1954.

name: Basilica of St. Stanislaus
facts: A center of Polish-American Catholic life in western Massachusetts.
Its large brick church anchors the historic parish community.
Designated a minor basilica in 1991.

name: St. Joseph Basilica
facts: A richly decorated church built by Polish immigrants in the early 20th century.
Known for its ornate interior, marble, and stained glass.
Designated a minor basilica in 1998.

name: Basilica of St. Adalbert
facts: The mother church of Grand Rapids' Polish community, completed 1913 in Renaissance style.
Its dome and twin towers are West Michigan landmarks.
Designated a minor basilica in 1979.

name: National Shrine of the Little Flower Basilica
facts: Built by the controversial radio priest Fr. Charles Coughlin in the 1930s.
Its Art Deco 'Charity Crucifixion Tower' is a striking modern landmark.
Dedicated to St. Thérèse of Lisieux; designated a minor basilica by decree of December 2014 (announced 2015).

name: Basilica of Ste. Anne de Détroit
facts: The second-oldest continuously operating Catholic parish in the U.S., founded in 1701 with the city of Detroit.
The current Gothic Revival church (1886) preserves relics of Fr. Gabriel Richard.
Designated a minor basilica in 2020.

name: Basilica of St. Mary
facts: The first basilica designated in the United States (1926) and the first in the Americas.
Beaux-Arts building constructed 1907–1914; co-cathedral of the Archdiocese of St. Paul and Minneapolis.
Hosts a well-known summer music and arts festival.

name: Basilica of St. Stanislaus Kostka
facts: A monumental Polish Cathedral-style church completed in 1895 above the Mississippi River.
Its great copper dome is a landmark of Winona.
Serves one of Minnesota's historic Polish parishes.

name: St. Mary Basilica
facts: The former cathedral of the Diocese of Natchez, built beginning 1842.
A Gothic Revival landmark on the Mississippi River bluff.
One of the oldest Catholic churches in Mississippi.

name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception (Conception Abbey)
facts: Church of a Benedictine monastery founded by Swiss monks in 1873.
Romanesque church noted for murals painted by monks of the Beuron art school.
One of the earliest rural basilicas in the United States.

name: Basilica of St. Louis, King of France (Old Cathedral)
facts: The oldest cathedral west of the Mississippi; the present church was dedicated in 1834.
Stands beside the Gateway Arch on the original 1764 site of St. Louis's first church.
Designated a minor basilica in 1961.

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Louis (New Cathedral)
facts: Seat of the Archdiocese of St. Louis; built 1907–1914 in Byzantine-Romanesque style.
Contains one of the largest collections of mosaic art in the world, covering 83,000+ sq ft.
Designated a minor basilica in 1997; Pope John Paul II visited in 1999.

name: Cathedral Basilica of the Sacred Heart
facts: Seat of the Archdiocese of Newark; a French Gothic cathedral built 1899–1954.
One of the largest cathedrals in North America, with 200-foot twin spires.
Pope John Paul II led a prayer service here in 1995; designated a basilica in 1995.

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi
facts: Built by Archbishop Jean-Baptiste Lamy (the model for Willa Cather's novel) beginning 1869.
Romanesque Revival in style, unusual among New Mexico's adobe churches.
Houses 'La Conquistadora,' the oldest Marian statue venerated in the United States.

credit.author: John Fowler from Placitas, NM, USA

name: Basilica of San Albino
facts: Anchors the historic plaza of Mesilla, near Las Cruces, a key site on the old Camino Real.
The present brick church dates to 1906, replacing an 1850s adobe chapel.
One of the oldest continuously active parishes in the Mesilla Valley.

credit.author: Original uploader was Camerafiend at en.wikipedia

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Victory (National Shrine)
facts: Built 1921–1926 by Venerable Nelson Baker as the heart of his 'City of Charity.'
White Georgia marble with a great copper dome; one of the first two U.S. basilicas (1926).
Fr. Baker, declared Venerable in 2011, is entombed within.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Perpetual Help
facts: A large twin-towered Redemptorist church in Brooklyn, a longtime center of the Our Lady of Perpetual Help devotion.
Serves a historic parish in the Diocese of Brooklyn.
Designated a minor basilica in 1969.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima
facts: Run by the Barnabite Fathers; centered on a large glass-domed 'Basilica' near Niagara Falls.
A 13-foot granite Our Lady of Fatima statue stands atop a domed globe over the shrine.
Surrounded by outdoor gardens with saints' statues from around the world.

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. James
facts: The oldest Catholic parish on Long Island, tracing to 1822.
Co-cathedral of the Diocese of Brooklyn; a restrained Georgian/Federal-style church.
Designated a minor basilica in 1982.

name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
facts: A large early-20th-century church serving a historic Syracuse parish.
Noted for its stained glass and devotional art.
Designated a minor basilica in 1998.

name: Basilica of St. Patrick's Old Cathedral
facts: New York City's original Catholic cathedral, dedicated in 1815 before the current St. Patrick's on Fifth Avenue.
Its walled cemetery and catacombs are the only ones in Manhattan.
Designated a minor basilica in 2010; featured in films such as 'The Godfather.'

name: Basilica of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary
facts: A shingle-style parish church serving eastern Long Island since the late 19th century.
One of the few basilicas in a small resort community.
Elevated to a minor basilica in the 2010s.

name: Basilica of Regina Pacis
facts: Built as a votive shrine of thanksgiving after World War II by Brooklyn's Italian community.
Its Renaissance-style interior centers on a Regina Pacis (Queen of Peace) shrine.
Designated a minor basilica in 2012.

name: Basilica of St. Mary of the Angels
facts: A Franciscan-associated parish in western New York, near St. Bonaventure University.
Known for its Gothic architecture and community heritage.
One of New York's nine minor basilicas.

name: Basilica of St. Lawrence
facts: Designed by Rafael Guastavino, the master builder who is entombed in the church.
Features a self-supporting tiled elliptical dome, one of the largest freestanding domes in North America.
Completed in 1909; designated a minor basilica in 1993.

name: Basilica of Our Lady Help of Christians (Belmont Abbey)
facts: Church of a Benedictine abbey and college founded in 1876.
Was once the only 'abbey nullius' (abbey-diocese) in the United States.
Its abbey church was designated a minor basilica in 1998.

name: Basilica Shrine of St. Mary
facts: Designed by Rafael Guastavino, famous for structural tile vaulting; completed 1911.
Its Spanish Baroque facade and tiled interior are architectural landmarks of Wilmington.
One of two Guastavino basilicas in North Carolina.

name: Basilica of St. James
facts: A Romanesque Revival 'basilica on the prairie' completed in the early 20th century.
Serves as a landmark parish in central North Dakota.
The state's only minor basilica.

name: Basilica & National Shrine of Our Lady of Consolation
facts: A major Marian pilgrimage shrine centered on a statue of Our Lady of Consolation brought from Luxembourg in 1875.
Draws tens of thousands of pilgrims each year, especially on the August feast.
Run by the Conventual Franciscans; a national shrine and minor basilica.

name: Basilica of St. John the Baptist
facts: One of the oldest Catholic parishes in the Canton area.
A substantial brick church anchoring the historic downtown.
Among Ohio's seven minor basilicas.

name: Basilica of St. Mary of the Assumption
facts: Serves Marietta, the first permanent U.S. settlement in the Northwest Territory (1788).
A Gothic-influenced church long central to the town's Catholic community.
Designated a minor basilica in 2013.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Mount Carmel
facts: A center of Italian-American Catholic devotion in the Mahoning Valley.
Known for its Marian shrine and festivals.
Designated a minor basilica in 2014.

name: Basilica & National Shrine of Our Lady of Lebanon
facts: A Maronite Catholic national shrine set on a hilltop in northeastern Ohio.
Features a large statue of Our Lady of Lebanon overlooking pilgrimage grounds.
Serves the Lebanese-American Maronite community nationwide.

name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Peter in Chains
facts: Seat of the Archdiocese of Cincinnati; a Greek Revival landmark dedicated in 1845.
Nicknamed the 'White Angel' for its gleaming stone and single tall spire.
Its interior blends Greek mosaics and murals; designated a basilica in 2020.

name: Basilica of St. Mary of the Assumption
facts: A historic parish church in Lancaster, in central Ohio.
Known for its Gothic Revival architecture and stained glass.
Designated a minor basilica in 2022.

name: St. Vincent Archabbey Basilica
facts: Church of Saint Vincent Archabbey, the first Benedictine monastery in the U.S. (founded 1846 by Boniface Wimmer).
Home to Saint Vincent College and Seminary; an archabbey, the highest Benedictine rank.
A Romanesque basilica at the heart of the monastic community.

name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Conewago Chapel)
facts: Conewago Chapel is the oldest stone Catholic church in the U.S. dedicated to the Sacred Heart (1787).
Founded by Jesuit missionaries; long a mother church of Catholicism in rural Pennsylvania.
Designated a minor basilica in 1962.

name: Cathedral Basilica of Sts. Peter and Paul
facts: Seat of the Archdiocese of Philadelphia; an Italian Renaissance cathedral built 1846–1864.
Its brownstone dome and copper lantern dominate the Benjamin Franklin Parkway.
Site of papal visits by John Paul II (1979) and Francis (2015).

name: Basilica of Sts. Cyril and Methodius
facts: Motherhouse church of the Sisters of Saints Cyril and Methodius, a Slovak religious congregation.
A center of Slovak-American Catholic heritage in Pennsylvania.
Designated a minor basilica in 1989.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of St. Ann
facts: Home of the St. Ann's Solemn Novena, which draws hundreds of thousands of pilgrims each July.
Run by the Passionist order in Scranton's coal-country heartland.
One of the largest annual devotional gatherings in the northeastern U.S.

name: Basilica of St. Michael the Archangel
facts: Stands where Prince Demetrius Gallitzin, the 'Apostle of the Alleghenies,' founded a frontier mission in 1799.
Built with support from industrialist Charles M. Schwab in the early 20th century.
Gallitzin's grave and shrine are on the grounds.

name: Basilica Shrine of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal
facts: Home of the Central Association of the Miraculous Medal, run by the Vincentians.
Its Monday Miraculous Medal Novena became one of the most widespread U.S. devotions.
Designated a minor basilica in 2022.

name: Basilica of St. Peter
facts: One of the oldest Catholic parishes in South Carolina's capital.
A brick Gothic Revival church in downtown Columbia.
Designated a minor basilica in 2018.

name: Basilica of Sts. Peter and Paul
facts: A Gothic Revival church, one of the oldest congregations in Chattanooga.
Its tall spire is a downtown landmark.
Tennessee's minor basilica.

name: St. Mary Cathedral Basilica
facts: The first cathedral in Texas; its brick church opened in 1848.
Survived the catastrophic 1900 Galveston Hurricane; topped by a 'Mary, Star of the Sea' statue.
Designated a minor basilica in 1979.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Little Flower
facts: A national shrine to St. Thérèse of Lisieux, run by the Discalced Carmelites.
Built during the Great Depression as a Romanesque/Byzantine landmark.
Designated a minor basilica in 1998.

name: Basilica of the National Shrine of Our Lady of San Juan del Valle
facts: A major Marian pilgrimage site in the Rio Grande Valley, drawing over a million visitors a year.
In 1970 a small plane crashed into the original shrine; the statue and Blessed Sacrament were saved.
The present basilica was dedicated in 1980 and designated a minor basilica in 1999.

name: St. Anthony Cathedral Basilica
facts: Cathedral of the Diocese of Beaumont; a Renaissance/Gothic church completed in the early 20th century.
Known for its ornate altars and stained glass.
Designated a minor basilica in 2006.

name: Basilica of St. Mary of the Immaculate Conception
facts: One of the oldest Catholic churches in Virginia and a historic African-American Catholic parish.
The Gothic Revival church was completed in 1858 and survived Civil War-era Norfolk.
Designated a minor basilica in 1991.

name: Basilica of St. Mary
facts: The oldest Catholic parish in Virginia, founded in 1795.
George Washington is traditionally said to have contributed to the parish's founding fund.
Designated the 84th U.S. minor basilica (announced 2018).

name: Basilica of St. Andrew
facts: A twin-spired High Victorian Gothic church completed in 1902, a landmark on a Roanoke hilltop.
One of the most prominent churches in southwestern Virginia.
Designated a minor basilica in September 2023, among the newest in the U.S.

name: Basilica of the Co-Cathedral of the Sacred Heart
facts: Co-cathedral of the Diocese of Wheeling-Charleston; completed in 1897.
A Romanesque/Gothic landmark in West Virginia's capital.
West Virginia's only minor basilica.

name: Basilica of St. Josaphat
facts: Built 1897–1901 by Polish immigrants, partly from salvage of a demolished Chicago federal building.
Its copper dome is modeled on St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.
The third minor basilica in the United States, designated in 1929.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Holy Hill (Help of Christians)
facts: A Discalced Carmelite shrine crowning a glacial hill northwest of Milwaukee.
Its Neo-Romanesque towers and scenic overlook draw pilgrims and tourists year-round.
A national shrine and minor basilica dedicated to Mary, Help of Christians.
